'''Kalappa Muniyappa''' (born 8 September 1952) is an Indian molecular biologist and geneticist, known for his researches on the chromatization of DNA and [[gene targeting]].<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=201 | title=Brief Profile of the Awardee | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref> He is a professor and chairman of the department of biochemistry of the [[Indian Institute of Science]]<ref name="K. Muniyappa on IISC">{{cite web | url=http://biochem.iisc.ernet.in/kmuniyappa.php | title=K. Muniyappa on IISC | publisher=Indian Institute of Science | date=2016 | access-date=9 October 2016}}</ref> and an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]].<ref name="Indian fellow - Muniyappa">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=P00-1282 | title=Indian fellow - Muniyappa | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=6 October 2016 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1995, for his contributions to biological sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Born on 2 February 1951 in the [[South India]]n state of [[Karnataka]], Kalappa Muniyappa, after graduating in science from [[Mysore University]] in 1974, secured his master's degree in 1976 from the same university with first rank.<ref name="Indian fellow - Muniyappa" /> His doctoral degree came from the [[Indian Institute of Science]] in 1980 after which he did his post-doctoral studies (1981–86) at the [[University of Georgia]] and at [[Yale University School of Medicine]]<ref name="Dr. Muniyappa Kalappa on Vidwan">{{cite web | url=https://vidwan.inflibnet.ac.in/profile/3648 | title=Dr. Muniyappa Kalappa on Vidwan | publisher=Vidwan | date=2016 | access-date=9 October 2016}}</ref> and returned to India in 1987 to join the Indian Institute of Science the next year as a member of faculty. He was made a professor in 1999 and is the incumbent chairman of the department of biochemistry of IISc. In between, he held visiting professorships at [[American Cancer Society]], [[University of Washington, Seattle]], [[Osaka University]], [[University of Sydney]] and the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council, London]].<ref name="Indian fellow - Muniyappa" />

== Legacy ==
[[File:Chording mycobacterium tuberculesis culture.jpg|thumb|235px|Chording [[mycobacterium tuberculosis]] culture - luminescent microscope image]]
Focusing his early researches on the molecular basis of homologous [[genetic recombination]] and employing RecA paradigm, Muniyappa demonstrated the effects of chromatization of DNA on homologous pairing and strand exchange and his studies are known to have assisted in exploring ways for gene targeting, cell senescence and genome stability.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=5 October 2016 | pages=32 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref> His studies on chromosome [[synapsis]], genetic recombination and [[telomere]] dynamics attempted to widen the understanding of cellular recombination and [[Holliday junction]] and he is credited with the discovery of a negative regulatory mechanism of homologous recombination.<ref name="Indian fellow - Muniyappa" /> His contributions in deciphering genetic recombination in [[mycobacterium tuberculosis]] are also reported to have influenced further researches on the mechanism of [[genetic exchange]] and [[lateral gene transfer]]. His researches have been published in a number of articles, 136 of which have been listed by [[ResearchGate]], an online article repository.<ref name="Muniyappa on ResearchGate">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/researcher/39912725_Kalappa_Muniyappa | title=Muniyappa on ResearchGate | work=Author profile | date=2016 | access-date=9 October 2016}}</ref>

At the Indian Institute of Science, he set up a laboratory, K. Muniyappa's Lab, to pursue researches in the fields of Cancer biology, Genetics, Biochemistry and Biophysics, where he mentors a number of doctoral and post-doctoral research scholars.<ref name="K. Muniyappa's Lab">{{cite web | url=http://biochem.iisc.ernet.in/kmlab/ | title=K. Muniyappa's Lab | publisher=Indian Institute of Science | date=2016 | access-date=9 October 2016}}</ref> Under his leadership, IISc introduced new academic programs such as the integrated PhD program, interdisciplinary program in chemical biology, and national post-doctoral training program in Biotechnology and Life Sciences. He served as their coordinator at inception.

A member of the editorial board of the ''Journal of Molecular Signaling'',<ref name="Editorial board">{{cite web | url=http://www.ccmb.res.in/index.php?view=ourteam&mid=0&id=62&grpid=39 | title=Editorial board | publisher=Journal of Molecular Signaling | date=2016 | access-date=10 October 2016}}</ref> he has also been associated with ''[[Journal of Biosciences]]'' and ''Indian Journal of Biophysics and Biochemistry'' as their editorial board member and has served as the vice president and secretary of the Society of Biological Chemists.<ref name="Indian fellow - Muniyappa" />

== Awards and honors ==
Muniyappa received the Hanumantha Rao Memorial Medal of the [[IISc]] in 1980 and the [[Rockefeller Foundation]] Career Development Award in 1992.<ref name="Indian fellow - Muniyappa" /> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1995. The same year, he received the M. Sreenivasaya Memorial Award of the [[Indian Institute of Science]].<ref name="M. Sreenivasaya Memorial Award">{{cite web | url=http://www.iisc.ernet.in/sbci/smaward.html | title=M. Sreenivasaya Memorial Award | publisher=Indian Institute of Science | date=2016 | access-date=9 October 2016 | archive-date=10 October 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161010214336/http://www.iisc.ernet.in/sbci/smaward.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> The [[American Cancer Society]] extended the Eleanor Roosevelt Fellowship Award to him in 1995. He received the Yamagiwa International Cancer Fellowship Award in 1999. The [[Indian Science Congress Association]] selected him for the Anima Sen Memorial Award in 2002. In 2007 he received the [[Indian Institute of Science]] Alumnus Award and the Kempe Gowda Award of the [[Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike]] (BBMP). He was given the Sir M. Visvesvaraya Award for lifetime contributions to Science & Technology by GoK, and the Karnataka Rajyotsava Award by GoK.<ref name="Indian fellow - Muniyappa" /> A founder member of the Karnataka State Academy for Science and Technology, Muniyappa is an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]. He was elected to The World Academy of Sciences (TWAS)<ref name="Fellow profile - Muniyappa">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Muniyappa,_Prof._Kalappa | title=Fellow profile - Muniyappa | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=6 October 2016}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]].<ref name="NASI fellows">{{cite web|url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=M |title=NASI fellows |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |date=2016 |access-date=8 October 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101227133632/http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=M |archive-date=27 December 2010 }}</ref>
